questions.q: What is the author's main claim?
options: China's demographic decline is now its single biggest weakness
China will collapse economically within a decade over its debts
China should now be seen as a bigger military threat than before
He now expects China to be less dominant, mainly because of AI
questions.explain: He is becoming a China bear: still powerful, but hegemony and tech dominance look out of reach, mostly because of AI.

questions.q: What does the author say was his earlier view of China's demographic decline?
options: It would force China to open its borders to migrants
It was the single biggest weakness holding back its growth
It never struck him as much of a threat to China's power
It would end Chinese growth entirely by around 2030
questions.explain: He says demographic decline never struck him as much of a threat.

questions.q: Compared with South Korea, China is described as:
options: Less industrial despite being less than half as rich
More industrial despite being more than twice as rich
More export-intensive despite being less than half as rich
Equally industrial despite being roughly twice as rich
questions.explain: The text says China is now less industrial than South Korea despite being less than half as rich.

questions.q: What did a senior transport official say in July about China's transport network?
options: It was running at a loss
It was 91% complete
It would be privatized
It needed to double in size
questions.explain: The Economist quotes the official saying the main network was '91% complete', with a pivot to upgrading.

questions.q: How does the author's view change his policy stance?
options: He drops military alliances but keeps friend-shoring and export controls
He now opposes export controls but still backs friend-shoring
He still backs the measures but with less urgency, like insurance
He becomes more hawkish and urges an immediate military buildup
questions.explain: He says the measures feel more like an insurance policy now, making him more of a China dove.
